ai.description: The Olive Ridley is a small sea turtle, reaching 60–70 cm. Its heart-shaped carapace is olive-green, and it is distinguished by having 6–9 asymmetrical costal scutes on each side.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Olive Ridley is best identified by its nearly circular, olive-colored carapace and the presence of 6–9 pairs of costal scutes, which are more numerous than in other species.
ai.habitat: The Olive Ridley inhabits tropical coastal waters, nesting primarily on sandy, open beaches of the Indian subcontinent, often near estuaries or mangrove-fringed shorelines.
ai.behavior: Olive Ridley turtles are famous for *arribadas*, a synchronized mass-nesting behavior where thousands of females emerge on the same beach simultaneously to lay eggs.
ai.reproductionNotes: Lepidochelys olivacea is oviparous, nesting primarily from November to April. Females lay 1–3 clutches per season, averaging 100–140 eggs each on Indian beaches.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Olive Ridley turtle nests along the entire Indian coastline, with major mass-nesting sites located on the sandy beaches of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
